newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean merchant banks to join in Jinro rescue.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean merchant banks to join in Jinro rescue.

text.p: A group of South Korea's 30 merchant banks have agreed to join the nation's commercial banks in efforts to bail out core companies of the troubled Jinro Group, an official for the merchant banks said on Monday.

The merchant banks agreed to join after commercial banks accepted their demand that they be exempted from granting fresh credit to the nation's 19th-ranked group, said the official at the Merchant Banks Association of Korea.

The Commercial Bank of Korea, the group's prime creditor bank, earlier said it would bail out flagship Jinro Ltd and five other subsidiaries of the group by deferring debt payments and offering additional credit.
Participation of merchant banks has been regarded as holding the key to a success in efforts by financial institutions to prevent this year's third major corporate failure.
The Jinro Group has said it would sell off some of its property and affiliates by the end of 1998 to raise cash to pay back debt, valued at 3.2 trillion won.
South Korean financial markets have been rocked by collapses under heavy debts of two leading steelmakers -- Hanbo Steel Co in January and Sammi Steel Co in March.
